diagnostic: S1 merger geometry: identity vs individual-image specialization
method: Per-image embeddings extracted from the frozen visual pipeline, base vs post-S1, held-out protocol (train exemplars/prototypes -> test). Levels: pre (final block features, mean pool), post (merger output tokens, mean pool), post_centered (post with global mean direction removed), pool (vision-tower pooler).

post.note: degenerate: constant direction dominates naive mean pool

post_centered.note: the tokens the LM receives ARE strongly identity-separable once the shared direction is removed

conclusions: Identity structure is NOT destroyed by S1: held-out 1-NN = 1.0 and prototype = 0.967 at every level, post-S1, including the LM-facing merger tokens (post_centered gap 0.715, base-identical). Case B (over-specialization / geometry collapse) is excluded.

The merger LoRA barely moved the output geometry at all (drift cos = 1.0000 post, 0.9948 pre/pool, the latter at numerical-noise level). S1's 0.64 train accuracy therefore rides on an extremely small, train-image-specific perturbation of the merger output rather than a reorganized identity space.

The tokens the LM receives already carry near-perfect identity information in the BASE model (post_centered 1-NN = 1.0). The binding failure is purely a readout/binding problem inside the (mostly frozen) language side, not a representation problem anywhere in the visual stack.

Implication per the pre-registered interpretation: the next lever is the training objective (make the binding signal explicit/salient - e.g. contrastive-style alias supervision, per-identity staging, or an objective that rewards identity-conditional token probabilities rather than sequence likelihood) rather than further scope/capacity sweeps.
Secondary implication: since geometry drift is ~0, scope ablations that only add vision-side plasticity cannot change what the LM sees in first order; this explains the flat S0/S1/S2/S3 plateau.
